title: Lemelin et al. (2021): water ice-bearing south-polar PSRs
credit: Myriam Lemelin, Shuai Li, Erwan Mazarico, Matthew A. Siegler, David A. Kring and David A. Paige (2021). DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.4646092. Derived catalogue: Lunario.
frame: GCS_Moon / D_Moon_2000; lunar sphere radius 1737400 m; original prime meridian 0 degrees. No DE ephemeris frame realization is specified in the archive.
projection: Output: geographic degrees, east longitude then latitude in [-180,180] / [-90,90]. Read directly from DBF Longitude / Latitude; no projected-shape conversion or datum transformation.
processingNotes: Each Point is the author-tabulated PSR representative location, not a measured ice pixel or a footprint. Preserve the published decimal coordinates without claiming that positional accuracy.

Positive Count_M3 is a count of published M3 surface-ice detections associated with the PSR, not a concentration, coverage fraction or resource estimate. Source association permits detections inside or within 280 m of a PSR.

Paper resolutions: approximately 280 m per M3 pixel and 240 m per PSR-mask pixel. Feature resolutionM reports the M3 sampling, not location uncertainty. observationUtc is null because per-point observation times are not in this archive.

Read only Name, Latitude, Longitude and Count_M3 from the DBF in original record order. Blank Name becomes PSR record N (archive record identity, not an asserted paper PSR number). Do not import hydrogen, WEH, modeled depth, slope or mission-ranking columns.

Do not display the supplied SHP polygons as measured ice extent. Their area differs from tabulated Area_m2; this extraction uses only published representative coordinates. Unknown ice coverage outside or within these associations remains unknown.

title: LCROSS Centaur: water detected in impact ejecta
version: Colaprete et al. (2010) detection; Marshall et al. (2012) impact location
license: Factual coordinate extraction only; publisher articles are not relicensed or redistributed.
credit: Colaprete et al. (2010), Science 330, 463–468; Marshall et al. (2012), Space Science Reviews 170, 69–96, DOI: 10.1007/s11214-011-9765-0.
frame: Mean Earth, selenocentric coordinates, as reported by Marshall et al. (2012). No transformation to the M3 archive datum is asserted.
projection: Geographic degrees, east longitude then latitude; original -48.7093 degrees longitude retained.
processingNotes: Manual factual transcription of the weighted-average Centaur location and impact UTC from Marshall et al. (2012), Table 3 / section 4 and section 1. Independent NASA NSSDCA impact table also reports -84.6796 latitude, 311.2907 east longitude (equivalent to -48.7093).

Published location uncertainty is 1 sigma: 115 m along latitude and 44 m along longitude. resolutionM remains null: these are location uncertainties, not a sampling resolution or measured ice footprint.

Colaprete et al. (2010) report water vapor and ice in excavated debris. This marker is a localized impact-water detection, not a surface-ice spectral pixel, crater-wide deposit, quantity estimate or sample-return measurement. value and unit remain null.
